article.story: BLACKSBURG, Va. -- — Ben Hammond scored 15 points and Virginia Tech pulled away midway through the second half for a 70-61 victory over Old Dominion on Friday night. Virginia Tech used a 13-2 run for a 56-42 lead with 10:25 remaining. Tyler Johnson made a 3-pointer and Isaiah Elohim scored the last four points during the stretch. The Hokies led by double digits for most of the remainder. Hammond made three of the Hokies' seven 3-pointers. Johnson finished with nine points to go with six rebounds, three assists, a block and a steal. Elohim, Jaylen Curry and Butta Johnson chipped in with eight points apiece for Virginia Tech (7-1), which rebounded from a 26-point loss to Oklahoma State on Sunday at the Charleston Classic. Bubu Benjamin scored 15 points for Old Dominion (6-2). Adante’ Holiman, Jared Turner and Kylan Howze added 11 points apiece with Howze snagging 10 rebounds. Virginia Tech took the lead for good with about three minutes left in the first half and had a 34-27 advantage at the break. It’s the first game this season the Hokies have been held to less than 80 points. Up next Old Dominion: hosts Drexel on Tuesday. Virginia Tech: at home against Mississippi on Tuesday in the SEC/ACC Challenge. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
